title: Lukas Van Riel
text:
I study how climate change, disturbances, and their interactions shape the distribution of tree species in Quebec, Canada — combining field work, large-scale forest inventory data (Quebec’s permanent plot network), and spatially explicit model projections to look at these processes across different timescales.
I’m a PhD candidate in the Forest Ecology lab at Université de Montréal, a BIOS2 fellow, and a member of the Centre for Forest Research.
My interests center on climate change effects on the biosphere, biogeography, and species range dynamics — with a particular pull toward disturbance ecology and ecological forecasting at large spatial scales.
Get in touch: lukas.van.riel@umontreal.ca

title: Lukas Van Riel
text:
My research
 Forest succession under a changing climate. A multistate survival model across ~12,500 permanent plots shows harvest intensity — not disturbance type — determines whether warming-driven shifts in forest composition stick or reverse.
 Landscape-scale trajectories. Trajectory analysis of forest simulations, with Natural Resources Canada, to trace how these dynamics play out across the broader landscape.
 Yellow birch under climate stress. Using dendrochronology and ecophysiology, I look at how Betula alleghaniensis responds to climate along a latitudinal gradient in Quebec.
